raw_comment: The Midwest, southeast and particularly eastern western states; all appear to suffer the heaviest of droughts while states on the coast seem to not suffer nearly as much droughts. It's important however, to realize three things aside from the ocean that this graph does not include in the key. Which are the Rocky mountain effect on the eastern west states, the effect of ice on Alaska. the Lake effect in the Midwest, and dessert effects in the southern states. These are the wonders of drought in the graph beyond just common visual interpretation. the differences all between exceptional. extreme, severe moderate and mild all have to be genuinely measured, as per the description some regions that show "drought' are actually getting more rain than some places labeled as "mild" because the date comes from regional averages. Similarly, I wonder how any surplus of precipitation is shown, or could be shown. There seems to be an exceptional drought in my own residential region (Northwest Ohio) which I wonder if is because of the lake effect of Erie. The visual itself could be called "Graphing Droughts in the US" or for a more comical approach, "Have you ever seen the Rain" from a famous song written by the band Creedence Clearwater.
